A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MaGS research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial methodological and presentational revisions.

before.justification: V1 reports original MaGS reconstruction results on D-NeRF and NeRF-DS, component ablations, mesh comparisons and interactive deformation examples.

after.justification: V2 reports original reconstruction, human-pose, ablation, simulation and efficiency results across D-NeRF, DG-Mesh and PeopleSnapshot, including supplementary results.

M1.justification: V1's DF-MLP/ARAP and RDF pipeline is substantially reworked around guide meshes, MPE-Net, RMD-Net and RGD-Net. Gaussian-relative deformation is retained conceptually, but learned mesh refinement, mesh-pose conditioning and normal-offset logical coordinates change the procedure. Mesh extraction also changes from the stated Marching Cubes approach to TSDF-based guide-mesh construction.

E1.justification: D-NeRF is retained, but NeRF-DS evaluation disappears. V2 adds the DG-Mesh dataset for ground-truth mesh evaluation and PeopleSnapshot for human novel-pose synthesis. Soft-body dropping, gravity/collision and SMPL-guided simulations substantially broaden the demonstrated scenarios beyond v1's dragging examples.

E2.justification: Compared with v1 Appendix Table 4, v2's 400x400 D-NeRF comparison adds DG-Mesh, SP-GS, Grid4D, D-MiSo and DynaSurfGS. New comparisons also evaluate Dynamic 2D Gaussians and avatar methods including Anim-NeRF, InstantAvatar and SplattingAvatar. The NeRF-DS comparison, including its HyperNeRF and NeRF-DS baselines, is removed.

E3.justification: V2 drops the 800x800 D-NeRF accuracy comparison while retaining 400x400 evaluation, and its D-NeRF tables report MS-SSIM instead of SSIM. It introduces CD/EMD mesh evaluation, SMPL-based novel-pose evaluation and efficiency protocols. Stated training settings also change, including densification from iterations 500–50,000 to 100–15,000; these disclosures do not establish that every retained experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: The existing RDF/hovering ablations are reworked into RGD/hovering controls plus joint RMD-Net and RGD-Net removal, with aggregate and per-scene results. V2 adds spatial L1-error analyses on D-NeRF and PeopleSnapshot and expanded deformation case studies. V1's illustrated incomplete-mesh failure cases are removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. Both present point estimates and averages across scenes.

E6.justification: D-NeRF result entries are replaced: v1 Appendix Table 4 reports 43.45 mean PSNR at 400x400, while v2 Table 1 reports 44.06 for the revised method/configuration, not a controlled same-protocol gain. V2 adds mesh, human-pose, ablation and efficiency results, including 70.18 average FPS. NeRF-DS scores and the separate original-Lego result column disappear.

T1.justification: The formal mesh–Gaussian mapping changes substantially. V1's normalized sigmoid coordinates, free displacement and area/Gram–Schmidt update rules are replaced by logical-coordinate interpolation, normal-direction hovering and revised learned parameter updates (v1 Eqs. 6–9; v2 Eqs. 9–16). These are different mathematical definitions and transformations, although neither version develops theorem or proof results.

C1.justification: The unified reconstruction/simulation objective remains, but the abstract and introduction redefine the main contributions around learned mesh-motion refinement, MPE-based pose conditioning and compatibility with ARAP, SMPL and soft-body physics. This substantially expands v1's RDF-centered contribution and ARAP-based simulation account.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations of simulation transfer through persistent vertex/facet correspondence and learned mesh refinement. It introduces a multi-object-interaction limitation and explains the Torus2Sphere exclusion from main averages. V1's detailed low-resolution and restricted-view failure analysis is replaced by a shorter viewpoint limitation; the general dependence on adequate viewpoints remains.

D1.justification: V1's two-stage implementation description and hyperparameter table are replaced by documentation for the revised networks. V2 adds architecture diagrams, positional-encoding and layer details, pipeline pseudocode, batch size 2, initialization with 50 Gaussians per facet and NVIDIA RTX 4090 hardware information. The project-page address is unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds a mesh-reconstruction related-work subsection and substantially expands positioning against methods including PGSR, DynaSurfGS, Dynamic 2D Gaussians, SplattingAvatar and D-MiSo. Its discussion distinguishes continuous, temporally corresponding meshes from point-based and independently reconstructed per-frame representations. These changes exceed bibliographic publication updates.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and methodology are extensively rewritten. Coarse dynamic reconstruction moves into expanded preliminaries, the former standalone simulation section becomes part of methodology, and the appendices are reorganized around architecture, configuration, pseudocode, visualization and benchmarking. Network terminology and the contribution narrative are substantially revised.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column layout, redraws the overview and pipeline, restructures benchmark and ablation tables, and adds network diagrams, error-map grids and simulation sequences. The anchored-versus-adsorbed motivation sketch is retained and relocated, while v1's Gaussian-trajectory and failure-case figures are removed.

improvement.justification: V1 supports mesh fidelity and simulation mainly through qualitative examples. V2 substantially strengthens this central evidence with quantitative ground-truth mesh evaluation, human novel-pose testing, broader simulation demonstrations and efficiency measurements, alongside much fuller implementation documentation. Removing NeRF-DS failure evidence reduces transparency, and Appendix F overstates per-scene EMD superiority relative to its own table. Nevertheless, the gains in validating and explaining the central contribution outweigh these drawbacks.
